stem:
Gauri compares the algebraic expressions $2(n+3)$ and $2n+6$.

When may she treat them as equal?

options.text: Call them "same value" as a label only, without checking values of $n$ or rewriting one expression into the other.
Treat them as equal after checking only $n=1$, skipping that equality must hold for every value of $n$ (or by a valid rewrite).
They are equal: distribute to get $2(n+3)=2n+6$, so both give the same value for every $n$.
Use the same equality test to decide whether two unrelated geometric figures are congruent.

teacher.key_rationale: Two expressions are equal when a valid rewrite makes them identical or they match for every letter-number value: $2(n+3)=2n+6$. Relabeling as "same value", checking only one $n$, or stretching the test to geometry congruence all leave this hinge.
